abstract: Some classic massively parallel reporter assays to study transcriptional regulatory effects of DNA sequence elements cannot readily distinguish these from post-transcriptional regulatory effects of the same element on RNA. Therefore, we developed an approach enabling assessment of DNA/RNA regulatory elements in parallel: Inferred Stability Optimized Massively Parallel Reporter Assay (ISOMPRA). ISOMPRA quantifies pre-spliced RNA to more directly assess transcription rate, and spliced RNA, corrected for transcription rate, to identify RNA stability-altering 3'-UTR elements. We benchmark ISOMPRA with both predicted enhancers and 3'-UTR elements, including regions containing autism patient mutations. We identify numerous functional enhancers and UTRs and discover a subset with high-impact mutations. We further show that failing to consider both potential transcriptional and post-transcriptional effects results in numerous possible false positives and false negatives. Finally, we adapt ISOMPRA for cell-type-specific in vivo use, enabling analyses of variants in specific cell types in the brain and measurement of regulatory impacts of in vivo traits, such as sex.
